questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How scientists measure the loudness of sound
Noise, how it affects us and ways to reduce it
Why listening to birdsong is good for our health
The history of car horns and traffic in India
questions.why: They talk about noise and ideas for making the world a quieter place.

questions.q: Which sounds does Georgina give as examples of noises that really annoy people?
options: Birdsong and the wind in the trees
Music and laughter
Children playing
Beeping lorries and road drills
questions.why: She mentions the beeping of a reversing lorry and someone drilling a hole in the road.

questions.q: According to Julian Treasure, why don't we notice the effect of noise?
options: Because we have got used to ignoring it
Because most noise is too quiet
Because cities are getting quieter
Because we wear headphones
questions.why: He says there's so much noise in cities that we get into the habit of ignoring it.

questions.q: What can background noise lead to, according to experts?
options: Better concentration
Hearing loss in children only
Stress and mental health problems
Stronger immune systems
questions.why: Neil says background noise can lead to stress and mental health issues.

questions.q: Why are trees grown by motorways?
options: To give drivers something nice to look at
To absorb traffic noise
To stop cars from crashing
To reduce air pollution
questions.why: Georgina says trees are grown by motorways to absorb the traffic noise.

questions.q: What was Sumaira Abdul Ali told when she started her work in Mumbai?
options: That wanting to control noise is a Western idea
That the police would help her immediately
That Indians hate noise
That car horns are only for safety
questions.why: She was told these are 'all Western ideas to want to control noise – Indians love noise!'

questions.q: What does Georgina say honking means for people in India?
options: It is only for road safety
It is a sign of anger
It is against the law
It is a way to express how they feel
questions.why: Georgina says honking is almost another language; people express how they feel with it.

questions.q: What did the police campaign in Mumbai do?
options: It banned car horns completely in the city centre
It gave large fines to drivers who honked their horns
It kept traffic lights red for longer if it got too noisy
It built new quiet roads outside the city for lorries
questions.why: If noise at traffic lights went over a certain level, the lights would stay red for longer.
